newsitem.title: THAILAND: Democrat Party ahead in Thai poll-TV projection.
newsitem.headline: Democrat Party ahead in Thai poll-TV projection.

text.p: Three television stations projected that the Democrat Party of former premier Chuan Leekpai was running ahead in Thailand's election on Sunday.

Their projections were based on vote-counting 90 minutes after balloting had closed at 0800 GMT. Earlier, a television station's exit poll released minutes after voting ended, had put the Democrats in a dead heat with the New Aspiration Party (NAP) led by Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.
Channel 9 television, which had projected a dead heat with 124 for the NAP and the Democrats in its early exit polls, said the Democrats were now set to win 136 seats against 117 for the NAP.

The election, said by analysts to be the most violent and dirty in two decades, is for 393-seats in the lower house of parliament. A total of 2,310 candidates from 13 parties are taking part in the polls seen as the closest in memory.
In its projection, Channel 7 said the Democrats were seen winning 135 seats and the NAP 112 seats. The Channel 3 television station put the Democrats well ahead with 129 seats to the NAP's 89.

The election was marred by violence and reports of bribery and initmidation, according to election officials. Pollwatch, the election watchdog, said at least seven people were shot dead and 10 others wounded in election-related violence.
